gancho: On Oʻahu, a baby is found on his mother's skirt in the shape of a piglet. Kamapuaʻa, the hog child, grows into a shape-shifter who can be a handsome man, a giant boar, a grunting fish or a patch of grass, steals the chickens of chief Olopana, and turns his own body into a bridge up a cliff. Based on Martha Beckwith, Hawaiian Mythology (1940), and W. D. Westervelt, Hawaiian Legends of Volcanoes (1916).
capitulos: The fish with a pig's name
